articles.title: Sphenoid sinus volume according to multidimensional pneumatization patterns: a cone-beam computed tomography study.
articles.authors: Matheus Kawana Couto, Maria Luiza Sastre Catija, Lilian Cristina Vessoni Iwaki et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize differences in total sphenoid sinus volume according to multidimensional pneumatization patterns and demographic characteristics using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). METHODS: A total of 200 CBCT scans from 200 individuals (100 females and 100 males; mean age: 37.15 ± 14.60 years) were retrospectively analyzed. Total sphenoid sinus volume was obtained by three-dimensional segmentation. Evaluated variables included sex, age, facial skeletal pattern, sellar-related, clival and lateral pneumatization, sphenoid sinus dominance, and intrasphenoidal septations. Group comparisons used non-parametric tests, and multiple linear regression was used to quantify adjusted volumetric differences across demographic and anatomical categories. RESULTS: Total sphenoid sinus volume differed by sex, age group, and sellar-related, clival, and lateral pneumatization patterns (all p < 0.05), but not by facial skeletal pattern, sphenoid sinus dominance, or number of intrasphenoidal septations. In the adjusted model, female sex was associated with lower volume, whereas incomplete sellar and complete sellar pneumatization, combined dorsal-occipital clival extension, and full lateral extension were associated with greater volume (adjusted R² = 0.586; p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses supported the associations with sellar-related and lateral pneumatization, whereas the clival association varied according to the analytical approach. CONCLUSION: Sphenoid sinus volume varied according to sex and multidimensional pneumatization patterns. Sellar-related and lateral patterns showed consistent volumetric differences across analytical approaches, whereas findings for clival pneumatization were more sensitive to the analytical strategy and should be interpreted with greater caution.

articles.title: Surgical anatomy of the hypoglossal canal - systematic review with meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Daniel Gondorf, George Triantafyllou, Panagiotis Papadopoulos-Manolarakis et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The hypoglossal canal (HC) is a vital conduit for the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) and venous structures. Variations in its morphology, particularly bony septations, can complicate skull-base surgeries such as transcondylar or far-lateral approaches. This study aims to provide a meta-analysis of HC prevalence, morphometry, and surgical landmarks. MATERIALS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted through December 2025 following PRISMA guidelines. Pooled prevalence and mean dimensions were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses explored the impact of sex, side, nationality, and study type. Leave-one-out analysis was performed to evaluate the source of heterogeneity. RESULTS: Thirty-three studies involving 10,132 skulls were included. The pooled prevalence of a typical (non-septated) HC was 60.39% (95% CI: 46.67-73.34). Variations occurred in nearly 40% of cases, including incomplete (18.85%) and complete (17.74%) septations. A significant discrepancy was found between study types: cadaveric studies reported a complete septation prevalence of 35.39%, while imaging studies detected only 9.03% (p = 0.0070). Morphometric analysis established the HC is located within a mean distance of 10.0-10.8 mm (95% CI: 9.12-12.11) from the posterior and anterior margins of the occipital condyle. No significant differences were observed based on sex or laterality. Substantial heterogeneity and potential publication bias through asymmetry test was detected. CONCLUSIONS: Structural variations of the HC are frequent developmental variants rather than rare anomalies. The significant under-detection of septations by imaging suggests that standard preoperative CT may overlook complex neural or venous partitioning. A 10 mm distance from the condylar margins may serve as a practical anatomical reference for individual preoperative assessment to avoid iatrogenic injury to CN XII during condylar drilling.

articles.title: Rare association of metoptic canal and Warwick's foramen in an adult skull - anatomical case report and embryological considerations.
articles.authors: Cezar Octavian Morosanu, Amy Manson, Alistair P Bond
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accessory foramina of the orbital apex are anatomical variants with potential radiological and surgical implications. Although individually uncommon, the simultaneous presence of multiple accessory foramina within the same orbit has rarely been reported. METHODS: During a routine osteological examination, a rare association of Warwick's foramen (WF) and metoptic canal (MC) was identified in the right orbit of an adult skull. Morphometric assessment was undertaken, and a review of current literature was also performed to investigate the characteristics of these variants. RESULTS: WF measured 2.94 (± 0.38) mm × 1.94 (± 0.33) mm, with a canal length of 1.03 (± 0.09) mm, whereas the MC measured 0.73 (± 0.18) mm in diameter and 2.28 (± 0.79) mm in length. Their distances from the optic canal were 8.55 ± 0.29 and 1.07 ± 0.18 mm, respectively. CONCLUSION: This case documents the rare ipsilateral association of WF and MC in the same orbital apex, highlighting the complexity of this region. Recognising these structures is important in radiological assessment, as well as in pre- and intraoperative settings.

articles.title: Anatomical variability of the femoral neurovascular bundle below the inguinal ligament: a cadaveric study with implications for vascular access.
articles.authors: Leon Smółka, Miłosz Strugała, Bartosz Pomianowski et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The femoral triangle is a key region for vascular access, but the spatial relationships between the femoral artery (FA), femoral vein (FV) and femoral nerve (FN) may vary below the inguinal ligament (IL). This cadaveric study evaluated the anatomical variability of the femoral neurovascular bundle at three predefined levels below the IL. METHODS: Twenty lower limbs from 10 formalin-fixed adult Polish cadavers were examined. Measurements were performed at three levels below the IL: L1, 1 cm; L2, 5 cm; and L3, 10 cm. The FA-FV relationship, FN-FA distance and anatomically defined safe zone width were assessed. Previously reported information regarding the position of these levels relative to the profunda femoris artery (PFA) origin was used solely for anatomical contextualization. RESULTS: The anatomically defined safe zone decreased from 11.73 ± 3.53 mm at L1 to 9.64 ± 4.04 mm at L2 and 2.32 ± 2.13 mm at L3. Significant FA-FV overlap increased from 1/20 limbs at L1 to 18/20 limbs at L3. L2 was located distal to the PFA origin in most limbs, whereas L3 was distal to it in all limbs, providing important context for interpretation of the distal neurovascular relationships. CONCLUSION: The topography of the femoral neurovascular bundle changes substantially within the first 10 cm below the IL. More distal levels are associated with increased FA-FV overlap, a narrower anatomically defined safe zone and greater anatomical heterogeneity. Individual anatomical assessment, preferably with imaging guidance, remains important when planning femoral vascular access.

articles.title: Morphometry of the interscalene triangle and its relationship with the brachial plexus trunks and subclavian artery.
articles.authors: Işınel Elif Çelebi Aydınlıoğlu, Servet Çelik
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The interscalene triangle (ISA) is a region located on the lateral aspect of the neck through which the trunks of the brachial plexus and the subclavian artery pass. The aim of this study was to obtain morphometric data, including area measurements, and to detail the ISA and its relationships with the brachial plexus and subclavian artery. METHODS: Following extensive dissection, morphometric measurements of the interscalene triangle and its relationships with the brachial plexus and subclavian artery were evaluated bilaterally in 20 formalin-fixed cadavers (17 male, 3 female; 40 sides). Measurements were obtained using ImageJ and a calibrated electronic digital caliper. ISA area was calculated using three methods. Measurements were statistically analyzed, including side comparisons. The relationships of the brachial plexus trunks, C5 anterior ramus, and subclavian artery with the anterior scalene muscle were classified into four types. RESULTS: The mean ISA base length was 9.11 mm, and the mean ISA height was 53.40 mm. The mean ISA area was 233.99 mm² with ImageJ planimetry, 245.34 mm² with the base-height formula, and 278.30 mm² with Heron's formula. The anatomical relationships were classified as Type 1 (75%), Type 2 (15%), Type 3 (7.5%), and Type 4 (2.5%). CONCLUSION: The position of the brachial plexus relative to the anterior scalene muscle and the area of the interscalene triangle show considerable variability. These morphometric data may provide anatomical information potentially relevant to interscalene block procedures, scalene muscle injections, and surgical approaches for thoracic outlet syndrome.

articles.title: Association of accessory anterior cerebral artery, accessory posterior cerebral artery and double origin of superior cerebellar artery from the basilar artery and P1 segment of fetal posterior cerebral artery.
articles.authors: Mohammed Assaad Alnafie, Samir Moualek
articles.abstract: The cerebrovascular system shows several variations, often incidentally discovered during radiological evaluation. We report the case of a 56-year-old woman who underwent a successful enucleation of an olfactory groove meningioma diagnosed by MRI. MRA and 3D modelling of the cerebral arteries revealed multiple variations involving the anterior and posterior circulations. Anteriorly, an accessory anterior cerebral artery arose at the junction of the left A1 and A2 segments and fed the right pericallosal artery. The English literature reported only one similar case. Posteriorly, we observed a left-sided fetal posterior cerebral artery and a hyperplastic anterior choroidal artery acting as an accessory posterior cerebral artery. In addition, the left superior cerebellar artery had a double origin from the basilar artery and the P1 segment of the fetal posterior cerebral artery. In our opinion, such a combination of variants is less common and deserves to be reported.

articles.title: Morphologic characterisation and anatomical variations of superior cerebellar artery in Indian angiographic cohort.
articles.authors: Vinod Singh Jatav, Abdul Muqueet Shaikh, Sneh Jain et al.
articles.abstract: AIMS: To identify and evaluate the morphological and anatomical variations of the superior cerebellar arteries by using Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA). MATERIAL AND METHODS: A total of 105 patients (67 males and 38 females) who underwent cerebral DSA included in this retrospective descriptive observational study (from 1st September 2024 to 31 October 2025). Angiograms were reviewed for morphological characteristics and anatomical variations of the superior cerebellar arteries. RESULTS: A total of 105 patients (67 males and 38 females), comprising 253 SCAs, were studied. Out of the 105 patients, 33 (31.4%) had duplicated SCAs, which were more common on the left side (14.3%). Of the 253 SCAs, 159 (62.8%) originated from the basilar artery, 13 (5.14%) from the P1 segment of the PCA and 81 (32%) had common SCA-PCA origin. Symmetrical SCA origin was observed in 77 (73.3%) of the 105 patients, whereas 28 (26.67%) patients had asymmetrical SCA origins. The mean diameter of the first segment of the SCA was 1.00 mm on the left side (95% CI 0.96-1.04 mm) and 1.01 mm on the right side (95% CI 0.97-1.05 mm). The mean length of the first segment of the SCA was 15.56 mm on the left side (95% CI 14.96-16.16 mm) and 16.57 mm (95% CI 15.86-17.08 mm) on the right side. Early bifurcation was observed in 43 patients (40.95%) with 12 on the left side (11.4%) and 23 SCAs (21.9%) on the right side. Interrater reliability demonstrated moderate to excellent agreement for categorical and continuous variables, with Cohen's κ ranging from 0.353 to 1.000 and ICC values ranging from 0.679 to 1.000. CONCLUSION: In this angiographic series, duplicated SCA and SCA-PCA common trunk origin were relatively frequent. Recognition of these variations enhance the safety of neuro-interventional technique and approach for micro neurosurgical procedures involving the posterior circulation.

articles.title: Ultrasound mapping of the radial nerve along the lateral humerus in children: safe and danger zones.
articles.authors: Gündüz Ercan Kutluay, Mehmet Ümit Çetin, Abdülkadir Sarı et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Absolute distances from bony landmarks locate the radial nerve in adults but change with growth. Using ultrasound, we mapped it along the lateral humerus in children, expressing its position as a proportion of the humeral segment. METHODS: In 102 children aged 3-13 years without upper-extremity pathology, four points were prospectively marked with ultrasound on the right arm: the lateral epicondyle (P1), the points where the nerve leaves (P2) and reaches (P3) the lateral cortex, and the greater tubercle (P4). The distal safe zone (P1-P2), danger zone (P2-P3) and proximal safe zone (P3-P4) were tape-measured and expressed as proportions of the segment (P1-P4). RESULTS: P3 lay at 51.2 ± 5.4% of the segment from the greater tubercle, not significantly associated with age (p = 0.326). From 3​​-5 to 12-13 years, the distal safe zone increased from 24.5% to 29.7% of the segment (p < 0.001) and the danger zone decreased from 23.9% to 20.5% (p = 0.009). In no child did the nerve's lateral course reach the distal ninth or proximal third, with margins exceeding measurement error; yet age and segment length predicted P3 only within ± 23 mm, a window as long as the danger zone. Intra- and interobserver intraclass correlation coefficients were ≥ 0.925. CONCLUSION: Absolute distances increased with growth, whereas the nerve's proportional position showed no significant age-related change. The distal ninth and proximal third, free of its lateral course in every child, are preliminary anatomical estimates requiring validation. Between them, direct visualisation or ultrasound identification of the nerve appears necessary.

articles.title: Reliability of Theia3D for tracking lower extremity joint kinematics during barefoot overground walking in children with cerebral palsy.
articles.authors: Amy E Barbuto, Katy Mitchell, Christina Bickley et al.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine the reliability of Theia3D for tracking lower-extremity joint kinematics during barefoot overground walking in children with cerebral palsy (CP). Ten children with spastic CP, GMFCS I-II, performed three sessions of overground barefoot walking while eight FLIR cameras recorded video. On average, sessions were separated by 12 days. Theia3D software, version 2024.1.17, model version 12.0.1, performed three-dimensional pose estimation using video footage to compute lower-extremity joint kinematics. Inter-trial variability, inter-session variability, and the variability ratio (inter-session / inter-trial variability), calculated using a variance-decomposition framework were used to assess the reliability of the data. Across all joints and planes, inter-trial variability was larger than inter-session. Average inter-trial variability was 2.89°. Average inter-session variability was 1.76°. Inter-session variability was < 5° for all joints and planes. Average variability ratio across all joint angles was 0.63, indicating inter-trial variability was higher than inter-session. Our results demonstrate acceptable, <5°, inter-session variability in overground barefoot walking using Theia3D. Inter-session variability was lower than reported in marker-based studies in healthy adults and children with CP, consistent with markerless motion capture removing marker placement as a potential source of between-session error. Inter-trial variability was higher than reported among healthy adults and children, consistent with increased stride-to-stride variability in this cohort. Areas of further work include assessing Theia3D reliability in children using assistive devices and against concurrent marker-based comparators. Our results support Theia3D as a reliable measurement tool for assessing overground barefoot walking in children with spastic CP, GMFCS I-II.

articles.title: Component-specific generalizability of reduced prediction equations for peak L5-S1 loading during dynamic lifting.
articles.authors: Mohamed Aziz Riahi, Denis Gagnon, Philippe Corbeil
articles.abstract: Predicting lumbosacral loading during dynamic lifting remains challenging because spinal forces cannot be measured directly during occupational tasks and are influenced by posture, movement, anthropometry, and neuromuscular control. This study developed reduced equations for peak L5-S1 compression, anteroposterior shear, and mediolateral shear and evaluated their performance in held-out participants. A secondary analysis was performed on 2,242 trials from 28 participants performing 15-kg box transfers. Reference-model L5-S1 force estimates came from an electromyography-assisted optimization musculoskeletal model. Candidate predictors included anthropometric, postural, kinematic, temporal, and trunk coactivation descriptors. Participants were divided into training and held-out validation subsets. Partial least squares regression and variable importance in projection scores selected predictors for ordinary least squares regression. Participant-level bootstrap resampling assessed selection stability. Prediction of reference-model peak compression in held-out participants yielded validation R2 = 0.68, r = 0.83, RMSE = 553.1 N, and MAE = 440.6 N, with a mean predicted-minus-reference-model bias of 105.0 N and 95% limits of agreement from - 960.0 to 1,169.9 N. In contrast, anteroposterior shear (validation R2 = - 0.30, r = 0.21, RMSE = 474.5 N) and mediolateral shear (validation R2 = - 0.01, r = 0.28, RMSE = 58.6 N) did not retain predictive performance in held-out participants. Compression also showed the highest bootstrap selection concordance (0.90), compared with 0.56 and 0.70 for anteroposterior and mediolateral shear, respectively. Between-participant predictive performance therefore differed across L5-S1 loading components: reference-model peak compression could be approximated from reduced biomechanical descriptors, whereas both shear equations yielded negative held-out R2 values. These findings clarify the limits of reduced-descriptor prediction across loading components.

articles.title: Evaluation of IMU-based gait event detection algorithms across common urban walking environments.
articles.authors: Jill Emmerzaal, Philippe C Dixon
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate event detection is crucial in gait analysis, as small timing errors can affect biomechanical outcomes. This study assesses the accuracy and timing error of inertial measurement unit (IMU)-based event detection algorithms for outdoor gait analysis across urban walking surfaces. METHODS: We used the NEWBEE dataset: 20 unimpaired participants walked through a sub-urban environment, we compared 21 open-access algorithms based on shank, lower-back and foot-mounted IMUs against pressure insole ground truth. Algorithms were assessed for detection accuracy and timing error, on (level ground, stairs up/down, ramps up/down, and curbs up/down). RESULTS: KielMAT achieved highest aggregate accuracy for initial contact, while Greene & McGrath was marginally better for foot-off. Greene and McGrath showed the lowest, near-unbiased timing error for initial contact (9 ± 27 ms), but a foot-off bias of 88 ± 38 ms too early, versus KielMAT's 130 ± 41 ms too late. Both algorithms performed well on flat, sloped, and pavement surfaces, but accuracy dropped substantially during stair negotiation (76%-88%) SIGNIFICANCE:: We recommend KielMAT for initial-contact accuracy and Greene & McGrath for initial-contact timing precision; neither reliably detects foot-off within clinical tolerance. Future work should target improved foot-off and stair-negotiation detection, and evaluation in populations with gait impairments.

articles.title: Effects of intranasal cocaine on thermoregulatory responses during exercise in hot environments.
articles.authors: Whitley C Atkins, Zachary J McKenna, Noah P Jouett et al.
articles.abstract: Cocaine use is associated with increased metabolic heat production, impaired heat dissipation, and elevated risk of exertional hyperthermia in hot environments. This study evaluated the effects of an intranasal dose of cocaine on thermoregulatory, cardiovascular, and perceptual responses during exercise in two different environmental conditions. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, healthy cocaine-naïve adults completed 60 minutes of cycling at a fixed rate of metabolic heat production (∼5.0 W/kg) following intranasal administration of either a cocaine (3 mg/kg) or a placebo (lidocaine) solution (3 mg/kg). Trials were conducted in a hot-humid (38°C, 40% RH; n=13) and hot-dry environment (41°C, 15% RH; n=10). Core and skin temperatures, whole-body sweat rate, forearm blood flow, cardiovascular responses, and thermal perceptions were obtained. Cocaine augmented the rise in core temperature in both the hot-humid (0.11°C, p=.05) and hot-dry conditions (0.31°C, p=.002) when compared to the lidocaine trials in the respective environment. When indexed to changes in mean body temperature, sweating and forearm blood flow responses were attenuated during cocaine trials in both environments (p<.05). In the hot-dry environment, cocaine elevated heart rate and rate pressure product (p<.01), suggesting increased cardiovascular strain. Despite heightened thermal load, participants reported lower thermal strain and less thermal discomfort after cocaine administration, demonstrating blunted perceptual awareness of the heat stress. A single dose of intranasal cocaine impairs sweating and cutaneous vasodilation, increases thermal and cardiovascular strain, and diminishes perceptual cues that prompt cooling behaviors during heat exposure. These combined physiological and behavioral effects heighten the risk of exertional heat illness among cocaine users.

articles.title: Comparison of 5% fixed-concentration CO2 inhalation and PETCO2 clamping for assessing cerebrovascular endothelial function: the role of shear rate normalization.
articles.authors: Erika Iwamoto, Koki Akanuma, Arata Tsunekawa et al.
articles.abstract: Although internal carotid artery flow-mediated dilation (ICA-FMD) is a promising noninvasive measure of cerebrovascular endothelial function, its wider application has been limited by the technically demanding end-tidal CO₂ partial pressure (PETCO2) clamp technique. We investigated whether a simplified fixed-concentration CO2 inhalation method provides ICA-FMD measurements comparable to the PETCO2 clamping method and whether shear rate (SR) normalization improves agreement between the two methods. Eighteen healthy young adults underwent ICA-FMD assessment using two 30-s hypercapnic stimuli: PETCO2 clamp (target ΔPETCO2 +9 mmHg) and fixed-concentration CO₂ inhalation (5% CO2 gas), in a randomized crossover design. ICA-FMD, SR area under the curve (SRAUC), and SRAUC above baseline (DSRAUC) were determined. ΔPETCO2 and ICA-FMD were lower during fixed-concentration CO2 inhalation than during the PETCO2 clamp method (6.9 ± 1.3 vs. 9.4 ± 1.5 mmHg and 3.5 ± 1.5 vs. 4.5 ± 2.1%, respectively; P < 0.05 for both). Normalization of ICA-FMD to SRAUC and DSRAUC eliminated the between-method differences (P > 0.05 for both). Repeated-measures correlation revealed a within-subject association between ICA-FMD and DSRAUC (rrm = 0.61, P < 0.01), but not SRAUC (rrm = 0.32, P = 0.19). Bland-Altman analysis showed that normalization to DSRAUC improved agreement between methods, increasing the intraclass correlation coefficient from 0.44 (95% CI, -0.02 to 0.75) for unnormalized ICA-FMD to 0.81 (95% CI, 0.57 to 0.93) for ICA-FMD/DSRAUC. These findings suggest that inhalation of 5% fixed-concentration CO2 can provide ICA-FMD responses comparable to those of PETCO2 clamping when differences in the shear stimulus are accounted for.

articles.title: The inspired-expired temperature gradient: a candidate bedside readout of airway gas-conditioning stress during invasive ventilation.
articles.authors: Shailesh Bihari, Ubbo F Wiersema
articles.abstract: Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is framed almost entirely in mechanical terms - tidal stress, strain and mechanical power - while the thermal conditioning of inspired gas is treated as a humidification housekeeping problem rather than a determinant of injury. Yet tracheal intubation abolishes most of the upper airway's heat- and water-exchanging capacity, and both inadequate and excessive gas conditioning provoke epithelial damage and airway inflammation in controlled animal ventilation. We propose that the breath-by-breath difference between expired and inspired gas temperature at the airway opening (ΔT = Tₑ - Tᵢ) is a physically simple, continuously available signal reflecting the heat the airway exchanges with each breath, and that the magnitude and trajectory of ΔT carry information about gas-conditioning adequacy and, plausibly, airway and lung injury during invasive ventilation. The same temperature difference has already been measured at the bedside in mechanically ventilated patients, but generally interpreted as a property of the humidification device or of ventilation-perfusion mismatch, rather than as a signal from the injured lung itself. Because expired gas temperature is also influenced by pulmonary blood flow and core temperature, these effects must be separated before any injury-related interpretation can be made. We outline the physiological rationale, existing measurement precedents, falsifiable predictions, and a staged approach to testing this hypothesis.

articles.title: Effects of Ischemic Preconditioning on Post-exercise Injury Biomarkers, DOMS, and Endothelial Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Yilin Zhang, Kai Xu, Hengzhi Deng et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute exercise, particularly at high intensity, confers physiological benefits but may also cause tissue injury. The protective effects of ischemic preconditioning (IPC) in clinical medicine have been demonstrated in some studies. This systematic review evaluated whether IPC applied before exercise can attenuate exercise-induced injury markers, muscle soreness, and endothelial dysfunction. METHODS: Five databases were searched for peer-reviewed English-language studies published up to 29 June 2025. Three reviewers independently screened records using participants, intervention, control, outcome, study (PICOS) criteria for eligibility and assessed the risk of bias using Cochrane Risk of bias (RoB) 2 and Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Multilevel meta-analyses with cluster-robust variance adjustments were used to compare IPC with control conditions, with pooled effects reported as effect sizes (ES). Publication bias was evaluated using Egger's test. Evidence certainty was rated with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: A total of 13 studies (3 RCTs randomized controlled trials, 9 crossover, and 1 cross-sectional) with 263 participants (243 male, 20 female) were included. IPC significantly reduced delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) overall (ES = - 0.92, 95% CI - 1.83, - 0.01, p = 0.049), but only when applied locally (LIPC, ES = - 1.16, 95% CI - 1.82, - 0.50, p < 0.01) at 24 h (ES = - 1.04, p = 0.048) and 48 h (ES = - 1.16, p = 0.03) post-exercise. A favorable pooled effect on flow-mediated dilation was observed across heterogeneous protocols involving acute remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC), an acute comparison of LIPC with RIPC, and repeated LIPC (ES = 0.98, 95% CI 0.11-1.84, p = 0.03). No significant effects were observed for total creatine kinase (total CK, ES = - 0.38, 95% CI - 1.26, 0.50, p = 0.32) or cardiac troponin following RIPC (ES = 0.08, 95% CI - 1.79, 1.96, p = 0.86). No significant improvements in total CK were observed for acute or repeated IPC, LIPC, or RIPC (p > 0.05). Meta-regression identified recovery time as a significant moderator for cardiac troponin T (β = 0.02, p = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis is the first to systematically find that the protective effects of IPC can extend to certain exercise-induced injuries. Pre-exercise LIPC attenuated DOMS for up to 48 h, especially after high-intensity eccentric exercise, and may provide some protection against exercise-induced endothelial dysfunction. IPC did not significantly attenuate exercise-induced increases in injury biomarkers, although protective effects may emerge at later timepoints. Overall, IPC shows potential as a protective strategy against exercise-induced injury in sports medicine. However, the magnitude of its effects, optimal protocols, and the reliability of chronic application require confirmation in larger, higher-quality studies.

articles.title: Combined high-intensity interval training and propionate supplementation attenuate ventricular remodeling and cognitive decline in a rat model of heart failure.
articles.authors: Kia Salimi, Masoomeh Alvandi, Alireza Imani et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Heart failure (HF) is a complex clinical syndrome characterized by progressive ventricular remodeling, chronic inflammation, and functional decline, often accompanied by cognitive deficits. Although pharmacological therapies improve symptoms, residual morbidity persists, highlighting the need for effective non‑pharmacological strategies. High‑intensity interval training (HIIT(and gut microbiota metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids, may benefit cardiac and cognitive outcomes, but their combined effects in HF are unclear. METHODS: Forty male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to control, HF, HF + Propionate (1000 mg/kg orally), HF + HIIT, and HF + HIIT + Propionate groups. HF was induced via subcutaneous isoproterenol injections (130 mg/kg over four days). A 6-week low-volume HIIT program (three sessions per week) after HF confirmation. Cardiac structure and function were evaluated by echocardiography. Systemic inflammation and cardiac stress markers (TNF-α, IL-10, CRP, and BNP), myocardial fibrosis, and spatial memory were assessed. RESULTS: HF induced marked ventricular dysfunction, elevated BNP and CRP levels, increased myocardial fibrosis, and impaired spatial memory. Both HIIT and propionate independently reduced systemic inflammation and myocardial collagen deposition compared with HF. The combined intervention produced greater improvements in ejection fraction and fractional shortening, increased IL-10, and reduced TNF-α. Preservation of spatial memory was observed only in the combined group (p < 0.01). CONCLUSION: The combination of propionate supplementation and low-volume HIIT effectively improves ventricular remodeling, reduces inflammation and fibrosis, and attenuates cognitive impairment in rats with heart failure.

articles.title: Developmental changes in the carotid body transcriptome accompanying the maturation of chemosensitivity.
articles.authors: Emma J Hodson, Yoichiro Sugimoto, Rahul S Manamperige et al.
articles.abstract: The carotid body (CB) chemoreceptors mature perinatally to regulate fetal cardiovascular and postnatal ventilatory responses to hypoxia. This maturation is associated with an increase in the sensitivity of the CB electrophysiological response to hypoxia (chemosensitivity): a process that is incompletely understood but critical to systemic oxygen homeostasis. Hypothesizing that perinatal CB gene expression changes would reveal candidate mechanisms for oxygen chemosensitivity, we studied the CB transcriptome in sheep, where perinatal CB physiology is well-characterised. Ovine CB-mediated cardiovascular reflexes are detectable in the fetus and mature between fetal days 120-145 (term), while sustained hypoxic ventilatory responses are established by postnatal day 15. We performed RNA-sequencing on sheep CBs at each of these stages, and adults, along with the superior cervical ganglion as an oxygen-insensitive control. This allowed us to define tissue-specific changes in the CB transcriptome correlating with chemosensitivity maturation. Progressive CB enrichment was observed in genes implicated in murine CB chemosensitivity, including potassium channels (KCNK9), mitochondrial complex IV regulators (NDUFA4L2, HIGD1C) and hypoxia-inducible factor-2α (EPAS1). Genes with this expression pattern were also enriched for regulators of diacylglycerol, particularly DGKH. Together, this builds a detailed picture of the CB transcriptional signature, with core features established in fetal life and conserved across species. We also observed down-regulated CB expression of genes encoding multiple metabolic pathways, including the tricarboxylic acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation and ATP/GTP consuming processes. Tissue respirometry confirmed depressed oxidative metabolism in the CB vs. control non-chemosensory tissues, suggesting that this bioenergetic phenotype may be important for chemosensitivity. KEY POINTS: The carotid body (CB) chemoreceptors mediate rapid cardiorespiratory responses to hypoxia that maintain systemic oxygen homeostasis, but mechanisms of oxygen chemosensitivity remain incompletely understood. CB-mediated chemoreflexes mature during the perinatal period, with increasing sensitivity of the oxygen chemosensory response. We performed RNA-sequencing of sheep CB across three perinatal stages and adults, enabling us to identify gene expression changes that correlate with functional state. We describe a CB transcriptomic signature that is conserved across species, established in fetal life, and correlates with maturation. This includes TASK1/3, variant isoforms of complex IV, and EPAS1/hypoxia-inducible factor-2α. We also found progressive CB-enrichment of diacylglycerol signalling genes, potentially signifying a role in chemosensitivity. The sheep CB transcriptome also revealed striking down-regulation of metabolic pathways, and respirometry on fresh tissue confirms low CB oxygen consumption relative to control tissues. Alongside known variants of mitochondrial complex IV, this suppressed metabolic state may contribute to CB oxygen chemosensitivity.

articles.title: Adipose Tissue Leptin Receptor Restoration Is Associated with Attenuated Hepatic Steatosis and Mitochondrial Remodeling in Obese Leptin Receptor-Deficient Male Mice.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Yoichi Ono, Simone Kennard, Jing Ma et al.
articles.abstract: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) activation has emerged as a potential therapeutic approach for metabolic diseases; however, whether adipocyte-specific leptin receptor (LEPR) restoration, which is associated with BAT activation, is accompanied by improvements in hepatic steatosis in severe obesity remains unclear. We investigated the effects of restoring adipocyte leptin signaling in a mouse model of obesity on hepatic steatosis and metabolic remodeling using mice with adipocyte-specific restoration of the leptin receptor (LEPR) on a globally LEPR-deficient background, a model previously shown to exhibit robust BAT activation. Adipocyte-specific LEPR restoration markedly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, accompanied by decreased hepatic triglyceride content and reduced expression of the lipid droplet-associated genes. Hepatic inflammatory gene expression, IBA1 protein abundance, and circulating levels of TNFα, IL-1β, and IL-17A were also reduced, accompanied by lower plasma AST and ALT activities. Genes involved in lipogenesis and fatty acid uptake were largely unchanged, suggesting that reduced hepatic steatosis was not accompanied by major transcriptional changes in these pathways. Instead, adipocyte-specific LEPR restoration was associated with hepatic mitochondrial remodeling, characterized by increased Ppargc1a expression, mitochondrial DNA content, TOM20 abundance, citrate synthase activity, and ultrastructural evidence of reduced mitochondrial size. These changes were accompanied by increased expression of fatty acid oxidation-related genes and elevated ACOX1 protein abundance. Although circulating neuregulin-4 concentrations were increased following adipocyte-specific LEPR restoration, hepatic phosphorylation of AKT, a downstream effector of neuregulin-4, as well as AMPK, CREB, and ERK remained unchanged. Collectively, these findings support a protective role for adipocyte LEPR signaling in limiting hepatic steatosis and liver injury in severe obesity, with hepatic mitochondrial remodeling and changes in fatty acid oxidation-related pathways emerging as potential features of this protective response.

articles.title: The Cardiac SERCA pump Improves Peripheral Glucose Transport Through a Protein Disulfide Isomerase-Dependent Pathway during Diabetes.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Zahra Maria, Shanell Shoop, Allison Campolo et al.
articles.abstract: Calcium handling has emerged as an important regulator of metabolic function, yet the role of cardiac calcium cycling in systemic glucose homeostasis remains unclear. We hypothesized that cardiac-specific overexpression of the sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca⁲⁺-ATPase (SERCA) pump improves whole-body glucose regulation by restoring glucose transport in peripheral insulin-sensitive tissues under diabetic condition. Transgenic (TG) mice with cardiac-specific SERCA overexpression and wild-type (WT) mice were made type 1 diabetic (Dx). Glucose transporters (GLUT) trafficking was assessed using a biotinylated photolabeling assay. To explore potential cardiac-derived mediators, we performed quantitative proteomic analysis of cardiac tissue of WT and TG mice. Diabetic WT mice exhibited a significant reduction in cell-surface GLUT4 content in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, which was rescued in Dx TG mice (p<0.05). Using SignalP and TargetP tools, we further determined that 16 and 32 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in ventricles and atria of TG mice (vs. WT), respectively, were potentially secreted. We further demonstrated a substantial increase in the expression of prolyl-4-hydroxylase beta polypeptide (P4Hb), also known as protein disulfide isomerase A1 (PDIA1), in the ventricle of healthy and diabetic TG mice (by 1822% and 1355%, p<0.001 and p=0.008, respectively). We further demonstrated an increased P4Hb level in the serum of diabetic TG mice (p=0.01). Furthermore, incubation with recombinant human P4Hb increased glucose uptake by 33% in vitro (p=0.03). These findings suggest that, under diabetic condition, cardiac SERCA overexpression partially restored glucose transport in peripheral tissues through cardiokines, such as PDIA1/P4Hb. Insights gained from this study could lead to the discovery of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for diabetic patients.

articles.title: Ferritin-Related Genomic Variants Are Associated With Elite Endurance Status in Chinese Athletes.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Xiaolin Yang, Yanchun Li, Yaqi Wang et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Iron storage is associated with endurance performance, and serum ferritin (sFer)-associated variants have been identified in the general population. This study aimed to characterize sFer concentrations in Chinese athletes, identify ferritin-associated genetic variants, and determine whether these variants and a weighted total genotype score are associated with elite endurance athlete status (EEAS). METHODS: sFer was analyzed in 441 Chinese athletes (20 [4] y; 216 men, 225 women) by sex and athlete status. Genome-wide association analysis identified top sFer-associated variants (P < 1 × 10-5). Allele frequencies were compared between elite endurance athletes (EEA, n = 257) and other athletes (CON, n = 439), and a weighted total genotype score was constructed to evaluate its association with elite athlete status. RESULTS: Subelite athletes had lower sFer concentrations than elite athletes (Beta = -0.361, P < .001), and females had lower concentrations than males (Beta = -0.870, P < .001). Forty-three variants reached suggestive genome-wide significance, and the previously reported variant rs1260326 in GCKR gene was replicated, with the C allele associated with lower sFer concentrations (Beta = -0.204, P = 9.8 × 10-3). Twenty ferritin-associated variants showed significantly different allele frequencies between the elite endurance athletes and CON groups. Among these, rs2529440 in NOD1 gene was associated with EEAS (odds ratio = 1.315, P = .013). The total genotype score derived from these variants explained an additional 3.89% of the variance in EEAS. CONCLUSIONS: Ferritin-associated genetic variants, particularly rs2529440 in NOD1, were associated with EEAS in Chinese athletes.

articles.title: Treatment strategies for pediatric unicameral and aneurysmal bone cysts.
articles.authors: Beatrice Jung, Franziska Stiglmaier, Sven-Oliver Dietz et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Treatment of unicameral bone cysts (UBCs) and aneurysmal bone cysts (ABCs) in pediatric patients remains heterogeneous. Although numerous surgical and minimally invasive treatment options have been described, little is known about the factors associated with therapeutic strategies in routine clinical practice. This study evaluated treatment patterns and factors associated with therapeutic strategies in pediatric bone cysts. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 42 pediatric patients treated for UBCs or ABCs at a tertiary referral center between 2016 and 2024. Demographic characteristics, cyst entity, anatomical location, pathological fractures, radiographic parameters, treatment modalities, recurrence, reoperation rates, complications, and radiological outcomes were assessed. Associations between cyst entity, anatomical location, pathological fracture, and therapeutic strategies were analyzed. RESULTS: Forty-two patients were included (22 UBCs and 20 ABCs). When anatomical location was categorized as humeral, femoral, or other, no significant difference was observed between UBCs and ABCs (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test, p = 0.547). Age at diagnosis, pathological fracture rate, therapeutic strategies, recurrence, and radiological outcomes also did not differ significantly between cyst entities. ESIN was associated with pathological fracture and anatomical location, whereas no significant association with cyst entity was detected. Active cysts were observed in younger patients, were located closer to the physis, had thinner cortical bone, and were more frequently associated with pathological fractures. Recurrence occurred in 10 patients, 5 patients sustained a refracture, and 21 underwent additional cyst-related surgical procedures, primarily as part of further cyst-directed treatment. CONCLUSION: In this cohort, therapeutic strategies were associated with anatomical and biomechanical characteristics, including anatomical location and pathological fracture, whereas no significant association with cyst entity was detected in this small cohort. No significant differences between UBCs and ABCs were detected in treatment patterns, recurrence rates, and radiological outcomes. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that anatomical and biomechanical characteristics may be relevant to treatment decisions in pediatric bone cysts in addition to histological diagnosis. Given the retrospective design and unadjusted analyses, these associations should not be interpreted as evidence of causal or superior effects of individual treatment factors. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Multisite Implementation and Outcomes of KineTransForma: A Faculty-Supervised, Student-Delivered, Community-Based, Goal-Directed Home Rehabilitation Program in Chile.
articles.authors: Paul Medina-González, Pablo Morales-Barrientos, Hugo Tapia-Gallardo et al.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Home-based rehabilitation for functional dependency is difficult to deliver at scale in settings where timely access to physical therapy is constrained. Pragmatic evidence is needed on feasible models that make implementation and outcomes visible under real-world conditions. OBJECTIVE: The objective was to evaluate the implementation and outcomes of KineTransForma, a faculty-supervised, student-delivered, community-based, goal-directed home rehabilitation program in Chile. DESIGN: This multisite pragmatic program evaluation used a nonrandomized pre-post design and was guided by the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework. SETTING: The evaluation was conducted at 3 community sites in a south-central Chilean region during the 2025 program cycle. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 42 dependency contexts were included, each defined as an adult with functional dependency or risk of dependency and the immediate in-home care network. Patients had a mean age of 65.29 years; 31 of 42 were female, and a primary caregiver was identified in 38 of 42 contexts. INTERVENTION(S) OR EXPOSURE(S): Supervised home sessions were delivered by physical therapy students under faculty supervision across semester-based fieldwork periods. Progression was anchored to the Critical Functional Context-Maximum Motor Milestone (CFC-MaxMM) and a therapeutic-window framework integrating task performance, physiological cost, and perceived exertion. MAIN OUTCOME(S) AND MEASURE(S): Implementation indicators included delivered sessions, total minutes, and caregiver involvement. Effectiveness outcomes were Barthel Index, Elderly Mobility Scale , manual muscle testing-derived global strength, and CFC-MaxMM distribution. RESULTS: Mean program exposure was 17.45 sessions and 1618.93 minutes per context. A formal caregiver was identified in 90.5% of contexts. Barthel Index, Elderly Mobility Scale, and global strength increased from baseline to postintervention, and CFC-MaxMM distribution shifted toward higher mobility levels. CONCLUSIONS: KineTransForma was feasibly implemented across 3 community sites and yielded favorable functional signals under routine-care constraints. RELEVANCE: These findings support the relevance of a pragmatic, milestone-anchored home rehabilitation model while justifying further study with stronger designs and follow-up.

articles.title: MIND diet adherence, incident epilepsy, and multi-omics signatures: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Yuxi Zhang, Yifei Chen, Siqi Ding et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dietary patterns are increasingly recognized as modifiable lifestyle factors relevant to neurological health, but their association with incident epilepsy remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: We examined associations between Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet adherence and incident epilepsy, using four other dietary patterns as comparators, and evaluated MIND-related food components, circulating biomarkers, and brain structural features. METHODS: We included 107,016 UK Biobank participants with at least two Oxford WebQ 24-hour dietary assessments. Cox regression examined dietary associations with incident epilepsy with sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Weighted logistic regression assessed cross-sectional associations between dietary patterns and epilepsy status in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Food components were evaluated using Cox regression and XGBoost with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values. Linear regression assessed MIND associations with metabolites, proteins, and imaging measures; elastic-net regression selected metabolites. Cox models evaluated metabolite and protein associations with epilepsy, and exploratory mediation models estimated indirect associations. RESULTS: During follow-up, 511 UK Biobank participants developed epilepsy. Each 1-SD increase in MIND score was associated with lower incident epilepsy risk (HR: 0.867; 95% CI: 0.791, 0.951), and NHANES showed an inverse cross-sectional association (OR: 0.772; 95% CI: 0.621, 0.959). Among MIND components, nuts showed the clearest inverse association. Multi-omics analyses identified 16 MIND-related metabolites, mainly involving fatty acids and lipoproteins. In the proteomic subset, 20 MIND-related proteins were nominally associated with epilepsy. MIND adherence was also associated with brain structural measures. CONCLUSIONS: Higher MIND diet adherence was associated with a lower risk of incident epilepsy, with nuts showing the clearest inverse association among individual components. Related metabolic, protein, and brain structural signals may inform hypotheses about biological links between MIND adherence and epilepsy risk.

articles.title: Ultra-Endurance Exercise Modifies Microbiota-Associated Amino Acid Metabolites Concurrent with Signs of Gut Barrier Injury.
articles.authors: Casey K Y Lim, Mikaela C Kasperek, Eleanor Eck et al.
articles.abstract: Extreme endurance exercise disrupts gastrointestinal function, yet its effects on microbiota-associated metabolism remain poorly understood. Microbial metabolism of aromatic amino acids (ArAAs) generates bioactive indole- and phenol-derived compounds, including aryl-lactates and aryl-acetates, with distinct and potentially opposing effects on host physiology. Building on our prior exercise-training work, we hypothesized that completion of a 100-mile ultramarathon would modulate both host and microbial-derived ArAA metabolites. Participants in the 2022 Western States Endurance Run (n = 40) provided stool and serum samples before and after completion of the race. Gut microbial composition was assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing, ArAA metabolites associated with both host and microbial metabolism were measured by targeted LC-MS, and circulating markers of intestinal epithelial injury by intestinal fatty acid binding protein (I-FABP) and lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LPS-BP). Microbial α- and β-diversity were unchanged following the race, although relative abundance of Streptococcus, Collinsella and Veillonella increased while Monoglobus decreased significantly. In contrast, alterations in ArAA metabolite profiles were observed. Serum aryl-acetates increased, characterized by increases in fecal phenylacetic acid (PAA) and circulating phenylacetyl-glutamine (PAG), whereas aryl-lactates decreased. Similar changes were observed in feces, characterized by increased PAA following the race and significantly different pre- to post-race changes in aryl-acetates versus aryl-lactates. Additionally, microbial tryptophan derivatives tryptamine and indole increased in feces but decreased in circulation following the race. Circulating I-FABP and LPS-BP also increased, consistent with intestinal epithelial injury. These findings demonstrate that completion of an ultramarathon is associated with alterations in microbiota-associated ArAA metabolism and increased markers of gut barrier injury despite minimal acute changes in overall gut microbial composition.
