articles.title: Riboflavin and vitamin A deficiencies are associated with poorer iron status in Madagascar.
articles.authors: Jocelyne M Labonté, Jean-Marie Rakotovao, Sonia Fortin et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Iron deficiency is a major contributor to anemia globally, but iron status is influenced by factors beyond intake, including riboflavin and vitamin A deficiencies, which affect iron metabolism. OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between vitamin A, riboflavin, and iron biomarkers, ferritin and soluble transferrin receptor (sTfR), among preschool children, adolescents, and women in Madagascar. METHODS: This secondary analysis used data from a national cross-sectional micronutrient survey conducted in Madagascar in 2024. The analysis included preschool children (PSC, 6-59 months, n=1692), adolescents (10-19 years, n=2857), and non-pregnant women (20-49 years, n=2493) with available biomarker data. Vitamin A deficiency (VAD) was defined as retinol binding protein (RBP) <0.648 μmol/L, marginal vitamin A status as RBP <0.897 μmol/L, and riboflavin deficiency as erythrocyte glutathione reductase activity coefficient >1.4. Ferritin and sTfR concentrations were natural-log transformed and analyzed as continuous outcomes. Separate multiple linear regression models were estimated for each population subgroup, adjusting for age, sex (as applicable), and malaria. RESULTS: In adjusted models, VAD was associated with 16% lower ferritin concentrations among PSC (p=0.003), 27% lower among adolescents (p=0.001), and 33% lower among women (p<0.001). Similar associations were observed with riboflavin deficiency, with ferritin concentrations 21% (p=0.01), 28% (p<0.001), and 27% (p=0.004) lower, respectively. VAD was associated with higher sTfR among adolescents (12%, p=0.01) and women (13%, p=0.01). sTfR did not differ significantly among PSC with VAD, nor with riboflavin deficiency in any subgroup. Marginal vitamin A status followed similar patterns to VAD. CONCLUSIONS: Vitamin A and riboflavin deficiencies were associated with lower iron status across population groups. Further experimental research is warranted to clarify whether these relationships are causal and to guide population-level nutritional interventions in Madagascar and beyond.

articles.title: Obesity and Associated Factors Among Chinese University Freshmen: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Huixian Zhang, Zhixin Chen, Xinyue Guo et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Obesity constitutes a major public health concern that adversely affects the physical and mental health of adolescents. This study used cross-validated elastic net regression and logistic regression model to identify key associated factors of adolescent obesity among freshmen cross-sectionally sampled at random, and inform targeted interventions. Methods: During autumn 2023 (September-November), 16,092 freshmen aged 16-19 years were recruited randomly from universities in China's seven city/provinces. Questionnaires were used to collect data. Obesity was defined based on body mass index (BMI, weight (kg)/(height(m))2). An elastic net model combining L1 and L2 regularization penalties (α = 0.5) was used to select variables. A logistic regression model was constructed to identify the significant key factors and their associations with obesity. Results: The adolescent obesity rate was 10.53% (95% CI: 10.07-11.02%) (males: 13.09%; females: 8.76%; p < 0.001). The logistic regression model included 29 variables selected by elastic net regularization, of which 18 dummy variables were statistically significant (p < 0.05), Key adjusted correlates of obesity were female sex (vs male, OR = 0.75, 95% CI: 0.66-0.85), paternal obesity (vs no, OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.14-1.82), small food portions (vs large portions, OR = 0.35, 95% CI: 0.26-0.47), very slow eating (vs fast, OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.46-0.73), rare physical activity (vs competitive sports, OR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.18-1.57), occasional breakfast (vs daily, OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.07-1.47), no romantic experience (vs Yes, OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.11-1.41), and lower water intake (vs high water intake, OR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.35-0.55). The model's apparent AUC was 0.666 (95% CI: 0.656-0.683). After Bootstrap internal validation, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.658, indicating modest discrimination; the corrected calibration intercept was -0.085, and the calibration slope was 0.957. Conclusions: Several demographic, behavioral, psychosocial, and familial factors were associated with obesity among Chinese freshmen; these associations do not establish causality and require independent confirmation.

articles.title: Body Composition Differences Across Therapeutic Groups in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Luis Enrique Sánchez-Diestro, Raquel Macias-Montero, Patricia Palomo-López et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Body composition may be a relevant determinant of metabolic and functional vulnerability in patients with colorectal cancer. This study aimed to investigate the association between different therapeutic strategies and body composition parameters. Methods: An observational, analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted in adult patients with colorectal adenocarcinoma undergoing active oncological management at Hospital Universitario de Badajoz, Spain, consecutively recruited between 1 February 2024 and 20 June 2024. Nutritional status was assessed using the Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA), and body composition was evaluated by multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). Fat mass, fat-free mass, skeletal muscle mass, bone mass, protein mass, total body water, visceral fat, and basal metabolic rate were assessed. Patients were stratified according to treatment modality: surgery alone, FOREST protocol, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, adjuvant chemotherapy, and combined neoadjuvant-adjuvant chemotherapy. Between-group differences were assessed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), with additional Kruskal-Wallis tests performed as nonparametric sensitivity analyses for departures from normality. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results: A total of 91 patients were included, with a mean age of 64.97 ± 9.92 years; 56 (61.5%) were men. Significant differences between treatment modalities were observed in bone mass (p = 0.023), protein mass (p = 0.002), skeletal muscle mass (p = 0.022), fat-free mass (p = 0.022), and basal metabolic rate (p = 0.039). Patients receiving adjuvant chemotherapy alone exhibited the lowest values for protein mass, skeletal muscle mass, fat-free mass, and basal metabolic rate, whereas those receiving combined neoadjuvant-adjuvant chemotherapy showed the highest values. No significant differences were observed in the remaining body composition parameters. However, after adjustment for sex, the between-group differences in skeletal muscle mass (p = 0.319), fat-free mass (p = 0.315), bone mass (p = 0.308), and basal metabolic rate (p = 0.429) were no longer statistically significant. Only protein mass remained significantly different across therapeutic groups after sex adjustment (p = 0.012). Conclusions: Although several body composition parameters differed across therapeutic groups in the unadjusted analyses, most differences were no longer statistically significant after adjustment for sex, with protein mass remaining the only significant parameter. Given the cross-sectional design, limited sample size, small therapeutic subgroups, and potential residual confounding, these findings should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating. No causal or temporal relationships between therapeutic modality and body composition can be established. Larger prospective longitudinal studies with appropriate adjustment for clinical confounders are needed to validate these observations.

articles.title: Income Poverty Misses Most Households Reporting Meal-Affordability Deprivation in Türkiye: Targeting Rules and Food Consumption Frequency, 2023-2025.
articles.authors: Salim Yılmaz, Ahmet Murat Günal
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: In 2025, 35.1% of Türkiye's population lived in households unable to afford a meal with meat, chicken or fish, or a vegetarian equivalent, every second day (meal-affordability deprivation, a single-item proxy for food insecurity). This study quantified how many meal-deprived households the statistical 60% poverty line misses, tested whether register-like rules identify them better, and compared consumption frequency between missed and other adults. Methods: Survey-weighted analyses used Income and Living Conditions Survey cross-sections (2023-2025; 76,693 household-years). Decision-tree rule sets, penalized logistic regression and gradient boosting were trained on 2023-2024 and validated temporally on 7861 households from 2025 not matched to earlier waves. Self-reported consumption frequencies of 57,899 adults (2025) were compared by g-computation; intake and diet quality were not measured. Results: In 2025, 68.1% (95% CI 67.0-69.1) of meal-deprived households were not income-poor (70.4% in 2023); 3.6 million children lived in them. At the line's targeting rate, rule sets did not outperform it (structural -0.9 points, 95% CI -2.5 to 0.7; register-like -1.3, -2.4 to -0.2), while models adding income identified 3.6-3.9 points more meal-deprived households (about 330,000-400,000 nationally) but fewer children. At similar incomes, non-poor meal-deprived adults ate meat, fruit and vegetables less often than non-deprived adults (gaps 25.5, 14.2 and 13.0 points, similar across education levels). Conclusions: The statistical poverty line, not a benefit-eligibility rule, misses most meal-deprived households; register-like rules did not close this gap, income-based gains were modest and sensitive to assumed misclassification, and flexible models did not improve targeting over a linear one.

articles.title: A Systematic Analysis of the 2020 Update of the Health Star Rating Nutrient Profiling Model.
articles.authors: Damian Maganja, Alexandra Jones, Eden M Barrett
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: To inform efforts to improve the Health Star Rating (HSR) front-of-pack nutrition label, we assessed the alignment of the HSR nutrient profiling model (NPM) with the Australian Dietary Guidelines (ADGs) and the Nova system to identify ultra-processed foods (UPFs). METHODS: This was a cross-sectional analysis of the 2024 Australian FoodSwitch dataset, comprising detailed nutrition and ingredient data for 24,710 packaged foods and beverages collected from Australian supermarket retailers, via in-store visits and scraping of online stores, in 2024. We compared ratings under the HSR system, using two different threshold cut-offs (≥3.5 HSR and ≥2.5 HSR), to classification under the ADGs (core vs. discretionary) and Nova (non-UPF vs. UPF). We then appraised nutrition information and ingredients lists to identify and describe reasons for misalignment. RESULTS: Classifications were aligned between HSR and ADGs for three-quarters of products (76% and 75%, depending on the HSR threshold). Alignment between HSR and Nova was lower (65% and 57%). We identified three main reasons for misalignment, similar for both comparator systems: low HSRs received for core/non-UPF products with a poor nutritional profile; high HSRs received for discretionary/UPF products due to offsetting in the HSR NPM; and high HSRs received for discretionary/UPF products with improved nutritional profiles relative to similar products. CONCLUSIONS: While some divergence is to be expected given the different approaches and purposes of each system, we also identified some important areas where the HSR NPM is not performing as effectively as it could. Improvements to the HSR NPM will support policy coherence in Australia to more consistently promote healthier dietary patterns.

articles.title: Association of Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone with Thyroid Nodules Across Different Drinking-Water Iodine Concentrations: Cross-Sectional Analyses in Chinese Populations.
articles.authors: Tong Zhao, Ya-Hui Li, Chun-Hu Li et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Some studies have linked higher thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels to a greater likelihood of thyroid nodules (TNs), while excess iodine exposure may increase TSH levels and the risk of subclinical hypothyroidism, suggesting that environmental iodine exposure may contribute to differences in the TSH-TN association. Whether this association varies across iodine-exposure settings remains unclear. We therefore examined associations of TSH with TN presence and nodule number and further explored whether they differed by drinking-water iodine concentration (WIC) level. METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled two analytic populations from Anhui and Shandong Provinces, China, for analyses of TN presence and nodule number. Study areas were classified as iodine-deficient areas (<40 μg/L), iodine-adequate areas (40-100 μg/L), or iodine-excess areas (>100 μg/L) based on WIC. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations of log-transformed TSH with both outcomes, including interaction and stratified analyses by WIC. RESULTS: In the TN presence analysis (n = 1189), 24.0% had TNs. Higher TSH was associated with lower odds of TN presence (OR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.59-0.98; p = 0.031), with interaction by WIC (p = 0.002). The association was evident in the iodine-excess areas (OR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.38-0.72; p < 0.001). In the nodule number analysis (n = 160), 30.0% had multiple nodules. Higher TSH was associated with higher odds of solitary rather than multiple nodules (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.02-3.70; p = 0.043), with no evidence of interaction with WIC (p for interaction = 0.944). CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the importance of considering environmental iodine conditions when interpreting TSH-TN associations and may help explain heterogeneity across populations.

articles.title: Thermal Responses During Sequential Carbohydrate Gel and Caffeine Intake Assessed by Infrared Thermography: Differences by Sex and Body Mass Index.
articles.authors: Zeynep Ercan Karakaya, Elif Günalan, Hayrettin Mutlu
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate infrared thermography (IRT)-assessed thermal responses during a sequential carbohydrate gel and caffeine protocol across body mass index and sex groups. We also investigated whether absolute supraclavicular temperature (Tscv) alone is sufficient to interpret brown adipose tissue (BAT)-related thermal responses and examined the contribution of reference-adjusted thermal parameters. Methods: Our study included 36 participants, with 12 individuals in each group: those with normal weight, overweight, and obesity. The experimental protocol lasted 120 min. Participants received carbohydrate gel, followed by 200 mg of caffeine at 45 min. We assessed Tscv, reference temperature (Tref), relative temperature (Trel), delta temperature (ΔT), estimated core temperature, blood pressure, and heart rate. Neither BAT activity nor energy expenditure was measured directly. The study was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07868302). Results: Mean Tscv increased from baseline during the carbohydrate phase (median increase at 45 min: 0.72 °C; p < 0.001), with no further significant change after caffeine administration. At 90-120 min, participants with obesity had lower Tscv and Tref than those with normal weight, whereas Trel, ΔT, and changes after caffeine administration did not differ, indicating differences in absolute temperature rather than in thermal responses. Mixed-effects models showed no significant time-by-group interactions. No consistent sex or hemodynamic differences were observed. Conclusions: Supraclavicular skin temperature may be influenced by regional adiposity and heat transfer and should not be interpreted as an independent indicator of BAT activity. Controlled studies are needed to clarify the utility of IRT in assessing diet-induced thermogenesis.

articles.title: How Common Are Meal Swipe Donation Programs? A National Study of Four-Year Postsecondary Institutions in the United States.
articles.authors: Sally L Bullock, Avery Foster, Ella Williams et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Meal swipe donation programs are a recognized campus food security strategy, yet little is known about their national prevalence or the institutional and policy-level factors associated with their presence. Methods: This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence of student-recipient meal swipe donation programs at 481 U.S. four-year postsecondary institutions using a systematic website-based audit. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine associations between institutional and policy-level characteristics and program presence. Results: Overall, 199 institutions (41.4%) offered a student-recipient meal swipe donation program, and 239 (49.7%) offered any type of meal swipe program. After adjustment, institution size showed the strongest association with program presence. Institutions contracting with Sodexo (OR = 8.86), Aramark (OR = 3.52), or Compass/Chartwells (OR = 3.55) were significantly more likely to have programs than self-operated institutions. Location in a state with a hunger-free campus policy (OR = 1.88) and a campus food pantry (OR = 2.47) were also independently associated with program presence. A higher percentage of Pell grant recipients was associated with lower odds of program presence. Institutional control, urbanization, and region were not significantly associated with program presence after adjustment. Conclusions: Findings indicate that meal swipe donation programs are present at over four in ten sampled four-year institutions, suggesting they are a relatively common component of campus food security efforts. However, program availability is unevenly distributed, varying by institution size, dining contractor, and state policy context. Expanding access may require targeted interventions, though more research is needed to evaluate program reach and effectiveness.

articles.title: Integrating Nutrition, Exercise and Personalised Care for Sarcopenia Prevention and Management in Older Adults: An Evidence-Informed Narrative Framework.
articles.authors: Edite Teixeira-Lemos, Jorge Oliveira, Ana Claudia Morais Godoy Figueiredo et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is a progressive, age-related condition characterised by declines in skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. It is associated with impaired mobility, loss of independence, poorer quality of life, and adverse health outcomes in older adults. Although nutrition is a cornerstone of sarcopenia prevention and management, its effectiveness is closely linked to exercise and to the individual's broader clinical, functional, and psychosocial context. This study aimed to develop an integrated, evidence-informed framework for sarcopenia prevention and management in older adults, with particular emphasis on the role of nutrition within a person-centred model of care. METHODS: An evidence-informed narrative synthesis was conducted to support a three-stage framework development process comprising targeted literature identification, evidence mapping and synthesis, and operational translation. Evidence was organised into key domains covering the clinical recognition and assessment of sarcopenia, the biological mechanisms underlying muscle decline, nutritional strategies, exercise, multimorbidity and medication-related factors, and personalised multidisciplinary care. These domains were then translated into an integrated, operational model of sarcopenia care. RESULTS: The synthesis identified interconnected biological and clinical determinants of sarcopenia, including anabolic resistance, mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, chronic low-grade inflammation, hormonal alterations, neuromuscular ageing, and the gut-muscle axis. Nutritional strategies addressing protein quantity, quality, distribution and timing, together with selected nutrients and dietary patterns, emerged as complementary components of management within an integrated approach that also incorporates resistance and multicomponent exercise. These findings informed a care pathway progressing from multidimensional assessment and clinical stratification to personalised nutritional, exercise and clinical interventions, with consideration of multimorbidity, medication-related factors and psychosocial determinants, followed by monitoring, reassessment, and adaptation over time. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed evidence-informed framework translates current knowledge of sarcopenia into a coordinated, multidisciplinary, and person-centred care pathway. Rather than replacing existing diagnostic or therapeutic recommendations, it offers a structured approach to integrating nutrition with exercise and broader clinical management, tailored to individual needs and goals. Prospective evaluation is needed to assess its feasibility, applicability, and potential contribution to integrated sarcopenia care.

articles.title: Exploratory observations of sleep during contest preparation in a natural bodybuilder: a case study.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.authors: Wassim Monastiri, Maher Souabni, Maïtena Saurel et al.
articles.abstract: Natural bodybuilders undergo prolonged caloric restriction combined with high training volumes in the lead-up to competitions to achieve extremely low body fat levels while preserving lean mass. Although sleep plays a critical role in recovery and metabolic regulation, its response to contest preparation remains under-explored. This case study followed a 24-year-old male natural bodybuilder across four months: off-season (AS-1) and a three-month contest preparation phase (AS-2 to AS-5). Body composition, energy status and sleep were assessed. The athlete lost 5.7 kg (6.6%) of initial body mass, including approximately 4.0 kg of estimated fat mass, reaching an estimated body fat percentage of 5.4% two weeks before competition. Energy intake dropped from 4345 to 2080 kcal per day, shifting energy balance from a 1159 kcal surplus at AS-1 to a 1052 kcal deficit at AS-5. Estimated energy availability progressively declined, reaching 23.9 kcal·kg FFM-1·day-1 at AS-5, below a proposed male-specific threshold for potentially low energy availability. Sleep quality deteriorated markedly: sleep efficiency declined from 93% to 83%, wake after sleep onset nearly tripled, and rapid eye movement sleep dropped from 30.8% to 4.4% at AS-4 and 12% at AS-5. Hypnograms showed sleep fragmentation and impaired REM transition. These findings suggest that sleep characteristics may vary during periods of severe energy deficit in bodybuilding contest preparation.

articles.title: Effects of a commercially available sugar-free energy drink on hitting exit velocity in experienced baseball and softball players: a randomized crossover trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.authors: Ian P Jump, Tahran Gotla, Madeline R Klubertanz et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Caffeine is commonly used as an ergogenic aid, with effective doses often reported at approximately 3-9 mg/kg; however, lower doses are also frequently included in multi-ingredient pre-workout supplements, and the effects of these supplements on sport-specific hitting performance in baseball and softball players remain largely unexplored. Thus, we investigated the acute effects of a commercially available, multi-ingredient caffeinated energy drink (ED) on hitting exit velocity, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, barbell velocity, reaction time, perceived energy, and post-running metabolic outcomes in experienced baseball and softball players. METHODS: Twenty-two experienced baseball and softball players (14 males, 8 females; mean playing experience: 13 ± 2 years) completed this double-blind, randomized, crossover study. Participants consumed either a sugar-free and caffeinated ED (C4 Performance Energy®; 5 kcal, 200 mg caffeine, β-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and vitamin B12) or a low-calorie, flavor-matched placebo (PLA) during two experimental sessions separated by ≥ 5 days. Testing batteries were performed at three within-session timepoints (T0: pre-consumption; T1: 30 minutes post-consumption; T2: post-exercise) and included CMJs, 30 back squat repetitions at 30% of estimated 1RM, a computerized reaction time test, and subjective perceptual questionnaires. Participants also performed 40 tee hits after T1 and before a high-intensity interval treadmill protocol, followed by 15-minute post-exercise indirect calorimetry. RESULTS: Both average (ED: 71.3 ± 14.0 mph vs. PLA: 70.1 ± 13.5 mph; mean difference ± SD: 1.20 ± 1.41 mph, 95% CI: 0.56-1.84, p < 0.001, dz = 0.85) and peak (ED: 76.7 ± 13.9 mph vs. PLA: 75.1 ± 13.6 mph; mean difference ± SD: 1.56 ± 1.70 mph, 95% CI: 0.79-2.33, p < 0.001, dz = 0.92) hitting exit velocity were significantly greater in the ED condition. A significant condition × time interaction was observed for CMJ height (p = 0.003), whereby jump height was maintained with the ED condition but decreased with PLA at T1. Post-exercise recovery energy expenditure was significantly greater with ED (~5%; p = 0.040, d = 0.46). No significant interactions were observed for barbell velocity, reaction time, or subjective perceptual questionnaires. CONCLUSIONS: Acute consumption of a caffeinated multi-ingredient energy drink resulted in small increases in average and peak hitting exit velocity and attenuated transient decline in CMJ height observed with placebo. These findings warrant future investigations with live-pitching conditions in prolonged game simulation settings.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of potassium-containing low-sodium salt substitutes for cardiovascular disease prevention in mixed adult populations: an overview of reviews.
articles.authors: Kirstin P West, Kokou Tbah Tighankpa, Zikang Fang et al.
articles.abstract: Potassium-containing low-sodium salt substitutes (LSSS) replace part of sodium chloride with potassium chloride to lower sodium intake and increase potassium intake. Yet, the review literature is overlapping and methodologically heterogeneous. This overview of reviews assessed the efficacy, safety, and evidence quality of potassium-containing LSSS for blood pressure, cardiovascular outcomes, and adverse events. Following a registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD420261294404), we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Global Health (EBSCO) and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews from inception to 6 March 2026. Eleven reviews met eligibility. Methodological confidence (AMSTAR 2) was high in one, moderate in three, low in five, and critically low in two, and primary-study overlap was very high. With LSSS, 24-h urinary sodium was lower by 9.41-35.82 mmol/d and 24-h urinary potassium was higher by 7.19-17.22 mmol/d. Review-level pooled estimates favoured potassium-containing LSSS for systolic (mean difference -4.00 to -8.87 mmHg) and diastolic blood pressure (-1.42 to -4.04 mmHg). Later reviews also reported lower all-cause mortality (RR 0.88-0.89), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.72-0.87), composite cardiovascular events, and selected stroke outcomes. However, these clinical-outcome estimates drew heavily on overlapping primary studies, particularly the Salt Substitute and Stroke Study, and are less independently replicated than the blood-pressure evidence. Serum potassium changed minimally (-0.02 to 0.18 mmol/L), with no clear excess of hyperkalaemia or serious adverse events reported. LSSS consistently lowered blood pressure; cardiovascular-event and mortality benefits remain promising but less certain. Trials outside East Asia with clearer formulation reporting and stronger safety data in higher-risk populations are needed.

articles.title: Low-sodium herb-enriched salt reduces blood pressure in children with excess weight: A Crossover Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Joana M Brandão, Diana B Cunha, Magno C Garcia et al.
articles.abstract: Excess sodium intake is a major modifiable risk factor for elevated blood pressure (BP), yet effective and acceptable strategies to reduce salt consumption in children remain limited. We conducted a crossover randomized clinical trial to evaluate the effects of a low-sodium, herb-enriched salt on BP in children with excess weight and their guardians. Child-guardian dyads (n=120) were randomized to receive either a low-sodium salt (65% NaCl, 25% potassium chloride, 10% anti-inflammatory herbs) or a placebo salt (regular sodium content) for one month, followed by a one-month washout and crossover. BP and spot urinary sodium were measured at baseline and after each intervention period. Analyses were conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle using mixed-effects models accounting for the crossover design. Among children, the intervention salt reduced systolic BP (-1.4 mmHg) and diastolic BP (-1.3 mmHg), whereas BP increased during the placebo phase (+2.5 mmHg systolic; +1.7 mmHg diastolic; time × treatment p=0.03 and p=0.04, respectively). In guardians, BP reductions during the intervention phase were not statistically significant. Urinary sodium decreased during the intervention and increased during the placebo phase among children, but the between-treatment difference was not statistically significant. Sensory acceptability was high, with over 75% of participants reporting that they liked the intervention salt. The low-sodium, herb-enriched salt was associated with modest BP reductions among children with excess weight and had high sensory acceptability. Longer-term studies are needed to determine whether these reductions are sustained and clinically meaningful.

articles.title: Ultra-processed foods intake and risk of Helicobacter pylori infection: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Kexin Li, Ziyuan Ma, Juanjuan Liu et al.
articles.abstract: Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) are closely associated with gut microbiota diversity and functionality. The gut microbiota plays a role in developing Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection. However, no cohort studies have explored the association between UPFs intake and the risk of H. pylori infection in the general population. In total, 1,769 participants without baseline H. pylori infection were enrolled in this study from the TCLSIH Cohort Study. Information on UPFs intake was obtained from a validated food frequency questionnaire, and H. pylori infection was diagnosed by using the 13C-urea breath test. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models adjusted for potential confounding factors were used to examine the association between UPFs intake and the risk of H. pylori infection. During a median follow-up of 2.0 years, the incidence rate of H. pylori infection was 20.92%. The multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HR; 95% confidence intervals) of H. pylori infection across increasing quartiles of UPFs intake were 1.00 (reference), 1.12 (0.79, 1.58), 0.84 (0.57, 1.23) and 0.86 (0.57, 1.29) (P for trend = 0.24) in males, and 1.00 (reference), 1.41 (0.74, 2.69), 1.49 (0.77, 2.88) and 2.72 (1.39, 5.33) (P for trend < 0.01) in females, respectively. This study shows that higher UPFs intake is associated with a higher risk of H. pylori infection in females, while no association was found in males. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Acute dietary stress during peripuberty impairs ovarian function in rat.
articles.authors: Pramod Kumar Yadav, Sada Nand Pandey, Shail K Chaube
articles.abstract: The quality of feed and diet during peripubertal period may have serious consequences during the onset of puberty, somatic and reproductive life. We aimed to investigate the impact of acute dietary stress on reproductive hormones levels, histoarchitecture of the ovary, and onset of regulated cell death pathways in the ovary of 32-day-old peripubertal female rats either subjected to complete feed deprivation (48 h) or kept on half diet (5 and 10 days). The body weight, relative ovary weight and histology, serum levels of follicle stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinising hormone (LH), and Estradiol-17β (E2), various autophagy and apoptotic markers in ovarian homogenates were analysed in the present study. Data revealed that acute dietary stress reduced relative ovary weight, serum levels of FSH, LH, and E2. Histological investigations suggest that the acute dietary stress significantly altered the histoarchitecture of the ovary, reduced the number of developing follicles, and induced regulated cell death pathways such as autophagy and apoptosis in follicular somatic cells and oocytes. The extent of ovarian damage was severe if the female peripubertal rats subjected to a half diet for 10 days. Taken together, these data suggest that peripubertal ovaries displayed increased susceptibility towards dietary stress leading to changes in hypothalamus-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis, depletion of the ovarian reserve, and compromised folliculogenesis due to induction of regulated cell death pathways. Indeed, nutrition plays a pivotal role in achieving sexual maturity in females, while peripubertal dietary hardships may affect ovarian function, delay puberty, compromise reproductive potential, and onset of ovarian diseases.

articles.title: Dietary selenium deficiency causes insulin-like growth factor 1 resistance in skeletal muscle of zebrafish.
articles.authors: Li Wang, Zixin Ou, Yifan Wang et al.
articles.abstract: Selenium (Se), an essential trace element for humans and animals, is critical for skeletal muscle homeostasis. Its deficiency is associated with low muscle mass due to the inhibition of the target of rapamycin complex 1 (TORC1)-mediated protein synthesis. However, the mechanism by which dietary Se deficiency hinders TORC1-mediated muscle protein synthesis remains unclear. Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1), a key upstream signaling molecule for TORC1, is pivotal in regulating muscle protein synthesis. This study evaluated whether dietary Se deficiency affects the transduction and transmission of IGF1 signaling in skeletal muscle using a zebrafish model, by manipulating dietary Se levels with Se-enriched yeast. Strikingly, dietary Se deficiency induced marked IGF1 resistance in skeletal muscle, characterized by elevated tissue IGF1 level but impaired transduction of both endogenous and exogenous IGF1 signaling from membrane receptor (IGF1 receptor/insulin receptor) to intracellular insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS1). Mechanistically, dietary Se deficiency downregulated numerous antioxidant selenoproteins, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, activated the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), and increased the phosphorylation of IRS1 at Ser307 and Ser312 sites, suggesting involvement of the ROS-mediated JNK-IRS1 pathway in dietary Se deficiency-induced IGF1 resistance. Overall, this study identifies a novel mechanism linking dietary Se deficiency to impaired muscle anabolism through redox imbalance-driven IGF1 desensitization, advancing the understanding of the role of Se in the regulation of skeletal muscle mass. However, the mechanism underlying the local IGF1 accumulation in skeletal muscle remains unresolved. Whether it results from reduced IGF1 degradation with unchanged muscle igf1 expression warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Association of the Family Nutrition and Physical Activity Environment with CVD Risk Factors among Kuwaiti Schoolchildren.
articles.authors: Abdulaziz Kh Alfarhan, Tyler B Becker, Karin A Pfeiffer et al.
articles.abstract: Childhood obesity and its associated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk are increasing globally, yet limited research has examined the role of family lifestyle environments in Middle Eastern populations. Kuwaiti children have been shown to have elevated CVD risk. To examine the association of the family nutrition and physical activity environment (FNPA) with CVD risk factors among Kuwaiti schoolchildren. FNPA environments were assessed using a validated parent-reported questionnaire in 356 Kuwaiti schoolchildren (mean age 10.4 ± 0.4 years; 52% girls) in a cross-sectional study. Anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, and lipid profiles were obtained using standardized procedures. Logistic regression analyses examined associations between FNPA score groups and CVD risk factors, with models adjusted for sex and, where applicable, BMI. FNPA scores were significantly lower among girls than boys (p < 0.05). High FNPA scores (>53) were associated with lower odds of obesity (OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.43-0.78; p < 0.001). High FNPA scores were also associated with lower odds of at-risk HDL cholesterol (OR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.28-0.76), low HDL cholesterol (OR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25-0.85), elevated TC/HDL ratio (OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.24-0.74), and at-risk triglycerides (OR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.34-0.96) after adjustment for sex and BMI (all p < 0.05). Lower FNPA scores were associated with higher odds of multiple CVD risk factors among Kuwaiti schoolchildren. These findings highlight the family nutrition and physical activity environment as an important context for early CVD risk, although the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation.
